en.title: Minimum Inversions When Merging Two Strings in Order
en.description:
Interleave two strings while keeping the original order of the characters within each string. An inversion is a pair of indices where the earlier character is strictly greater than the later one; find the minimum number of inversions after merging. For the source's zc and qd, the optimum under this definition is 4, not 2.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, and judging.
en.input: Two lines of lowercase strings, each of length 1..1000.
en.explanation: Example 1: merging into qdzc gives four inversions (q,d), (q,c), (d,c), (z,c), which is optimal; the source's 2 does not match the all-index-pairs definition. Example 2: merging into ab gives 0. Example 3: merging into aba gives only one inversion, (b,a).
hints: Let dp[i,j] be the minimum number of inversions after using the first i and j characters. When a character is appended, the new inversions equal the number of characters larger than it in the two used prefixes; precompute, for each prefix, the count of larger characters for all 26 letters, and use a rolling DP.
